name: Baha' al-Din Zuhayr
bio: Abu al-Fadl Zuhayr ibn Muhammad al-Muhallabi, called Baha' al-Din, was born in Mecca in 581 AH (1186 CE) and grew up in Qus in Upper Egypt. He became one of the closest secretaries of the Ayyubid prince al-Salih Ayyub, followed him to the eastern provinces and to Damascus, and when al-Salih's army deserted him and he was held at al-Karak, Zuhayr waited for him in Nablus rather than serve anyone else. His friend Ibn Khallikan wrote that “all his poetry is graceful; it is, as they say, the easy that cannot be imitated”, and al-Zirikli that he made his verse delicate, “so that the common people admired it and the elite found it charming”. After al-Salih's death he kept to his house, and he died in Cairo in an epidemic in 656 AH (1258 CE).
